svg.text: V3 Logistics Platform — Initial Building Blocks
Discussion draft assembled from round-1 Slack notes (James Kotze, Andrei, Hendrik) · for round-2 architecture review · NOT a final design
EDGE / ROUTING — CONTESTED, TWO PATHS PROPOSED
PATH A — Gateway / Load Balancer (proposed baseline)
compliance routing is the GW's job
"What if we didn't need a load
UNRESOLVED — pick a path before gateway responsibilities, WS handling, and rate-limit enforcement can be finalized
AUTH — checkpoint before the backbone (queried by the Gateway on Path A; still needed if Path B ever ships)
Surfaced once in chat, no follow-up — confirm adoption before assuming it's decided
Zanzibar / OpenFGA-style: tenant / organization / user / role / document relation tuples — membership inferred
NATS NSC scoped signing keys were evaluated and rejected as too coarse for this — FGA is meant to cover the gap
Directly answers the earlier "who can see what" unknown for tenants / users / roles / businesses
COMMS BACKBONE — the spine everything else depends on
Single message backbone for the whole platform
before it carries all of V3
SERVICES — candidate list only, none designed yet
Each service: own VM, own Docker container, Java or Go (language choice not confirmed per-service vs. platform-wide)
PERSISTENCE — cross-cutting, sits under every service
Postgres · NATS KV · JetStream — responsibility split not yet settled
Not discussed on this Slack thread at the platform level. This is the exact question this nats-tech-lab
repo runs Shapes A/B/C to answer for the Dictionary service — round 2 should treat those findings as input,
not a separate decision made from scratch per-service.

tenant) not yet evaluated — see AuthZ

Gateway job, not the LB's — but only

REGIONS: LB / Gateway / Services layers are assumed multi-region (global GCP LB, per-region backend MIGs) — which regions, and under what residency rules, is not yet confirmed.
